El primer mensaje de Schnorr es un <stro: Schnorr's first message is a commitment: it fixes a choice without revealing it. With a hash function it can be done with anything: to commit to a value $v$ you publish $H(n \Vert v)$, where $n$ is a large random number. Nobody can know $v$ (the function is not inverted, and the $n$ prevents trying candidates), and nobody can open the envelope with another value (you would have to find a collision). It is a sealed envelope that can be sent over the internet.
El protocolo de Schnorr convertido en fi: The Schnorr protocol turned into a signature with Fiat and Shamir's trick, replacing Victor's challenge with a hash, is the signature of modern curves. General zero-knowledge proofs, which prove any computable statement, have been used since 2016 in blockchains to validate transactions without revealing them, and are beginning to be used to prove age or nationality without showing the whole document. Commitments are in sealed-bid electronic auctions, in online games that draw lots without a referee, and in every protocol where somebody has to choose before knowing.
